definition: a piece of land almost surrounded by water.
example: Cape York is a large peninsula in northern Queensland.
originNote: from words meaning almost and island
spellingTip: Remember penin- has one n, then su, then la.

definition: an area of high, fairly level land.
example: The hikers crossed the rocky plateau before sunset.
spellingTip: The ending is -eau, sounding like oh.

definition: a very high natural rise of land.
example: Snow covered the top of the mountain all winter.
originNote: from a word meaning hill or mount
spellingTip: Mount + ain; don't forget the ai in the second part.

definition: a low area of land between hills or mountains.
example: A river wound through the green valley below.
originNote: from a word meaning low land

definition: a very dry area with little rainfall.
example: Camels are well suited to life in the desert.
originNote: from a word meaning abandoned place
spellingTip: For the landform, use one s in the middle.

definition: a large slow-moving mass of ice.
example: The glacier carved the valley over thousands of years.
spellingTip: The tricky part is -cier, which sounds like seer.

definition: a mountain or hill that can erupt with lava.
example: The volcano sent ash high into the sky.
originNote: named after Vulcan, Roman god of fire
spellingTip: Vol-ca-no: keep the c before the a.

definition: a deep narrow valley with steep sides.
example: We looked down into the canyon from the lookout.
originNote: from a word meaning tube or gorge
spellingTip: The middle sound is y, so write can-yon.

definition: a sheltered place where boats can anchor safely.
example: Fishing boats returned to the harbour at dusk.
originNote: from a word meaning shelter or lodging
spellingTip: In Australian spelling, remember the ou in harbour.

definition: an imaginary line around Earth halfway between the poles.
example: Countries near the equator often have warm climates.
spellingTip: After e, write qua like in equal and quantity.

definition: half of the Earth or half of a sphere.
example: Australia lies in the Southern Hemisphere.
originNote: hemi means half and sphere means ball
spellingTip: Remember hemi for half, then sphere with ph.

definition: the distance east or west measured from the prime meridian.
example: The map showed the ship's longitude and latitude.
spellingTip: It starts with long-, like length and long.

definition: the distance north or south measured from the equator.
example: Brisbane and Perth are at different latitudes.
spellingTip: Latitude has lati-, not latti- or late-.

definition: an area of land formed where a river splits near its mouth.
example: Rich farmland spread across the river delta.
originNote: named after the Greek letter shape
spellingTip: Keep the short e sound: del-ta.

definition: relating to the land beside the sea.
example: Many people live in coastal towns along the east.

definition: relating to the hot regions near the equator.
example: Cairns has a tropical climate with wet summers.
spellingTip: Tropic + al makes tropical; keep the c.

definition: situated in or facing the south.
example: Penguins live in many southern regions.
spellingTip: The th stays, even though it sounds softened.

definition: situated in or facing the north.
example: The Northern Territory is in the northern part of Australia.

definition: the physical features and shape of an area of land.
example: The rough terrain made the walk more difficult.
originNote: from a word meaning land or ground
spellingTip: The ending is -rain, like rain from the sky.
